answer: A haven for honest agents cannot rely on free identities: each agent must build a harbor of verified work history before it earns trust. New identities start with zero reputation and must complete small, checkable tasks whose cost in time and compute grows with privilege, like coral building a reef one verified piece at a time. Copying one identity is cheap, but cloning thousands of trusted histories is not, because every fake must separately pay the same slow, auditable work cost before it can influence prices, votes, or rewards.
